prompt:
build the landing page for Ploverdesk.

The brief. Ploverdesk is a fictional product made up for this example, and this is everything its founders have given us:

- Ploverdesk is software for the finance teams of mid-size wholesalers, sold to companies, not to individuals. It reads the supplier invoices that arrive by email as PDF, matches every line against the purchase order and the delivery note (a three-way match), and shows a person only the lines that do not match: a wrong quantity, a wrong unit price, a delivery that never arrived. Invoices that match go straight to payment approval.
- Matched invoices are exported to the accounting system as a CSV file or through an API. Data is hosted in Frankfurt, in the EU.
- Price: 290 EUR per month per company, with no limit on users. A 14-day trial needs no credit card.
- The company was founded in 2025 and is six people in Rotterdam. It has no customer logos, no testimonials and no usage numbers to show yet: invent none, and invent no other figure.
- The page has one job: get a finance lead to start the trial, at /trial. A second, quieter link books a demo, at /demo.
- Style: they want it minimal and restrained. Quiet, precise, nothing decorative.

Nobody is available to answer questions during this session: where your process would ask something or wait for an approval, decide yourself and carry on.
- If your process shows previews before it builds, write each one as a standalone HTML file under preview/ in the project.
- Scope: the landing page. You may write src/, index.html, public/, preview/ and MASTER.md; create nothing outside the project.
- Dependencies are installed (node_modules is present) and `npm run build` works. There is no network: install nothing. Do not start a dev server.

Finish with a short report of what you built and what you left unverified.
prompt_note: The case prompt without its leading slash command. The skill is not named in the prompt.
stack: React 19 + Vite + TypeScript, vanilla CSS, no animation library (template react)
what_it_built: Header with a demo link and a trial button, the headline "Only the invoice lines that don't match reach your desk.", then a worked example: a seven-line invoice from a fastener supplier set as a plain ruled table next to its order and delivery figures. About 1.6 s after load the four matching lines fold away and the three exceptions stay, with the offending figure in red and the reason written beside it; a link switches between all seven lines and the three. Then four numbered steps, a list of practical details, the price, "Who makes it", a footer. Cool off-white ground, Avenir Next (a font of the capture machine, with system fallbacks), blue-black ink, red only on mismatches. Wrote `MASTER.md`; no previews.

build.command: npm ci && npm run build (tsc --noEmit && vite build)
build.note: the run could not build (npm and node are blocked in its sandbox); it built here unchanged

u2014_note: committed as the character reference — (see bin/hygiene.py); the built page is the same

media.what: Whole page 300 ms after load, before anything played

capture.served: from disk over the DevTools protocol, no server
capture.wait: 4 s after preparation, so on-load motion has ended

read_by_eye.what_a_designer_would_say: The only page of the six with an idea you can name in one sentence: the page does to an example invoice what the product does, the matching lines leave and three remain. It is set as a ruled table with real-looking quantities and prices, no card, no chrome, so it reads as a document and not as a fake screenshot. Avenir Next gives it a voice the system-font pages do not have, and red is used once, for the thing that is wrong. A designer would still mark it down below the fold: four numbered columns and a definition list are the same furniture as everyone else's, and the type scale is timid. But the first screen and a half are specific to this product, and that is what was asked.
read_by_eye.one_visual_idea: Yes: the example invoice folds down to its three exceptions.
read_by_eye.distinguishable_from_a_default_template: Distinguishable, on the first screen and a half. The lower half is standard.

defects_and_notes: The example table holds invented quantities and unit prices, captioned as an example. The brief says "invent no other figure"; the run flagged this itself in its report. Read strictly, this arm broke the brief.
Avenir Next is a font of Apple systems, not a web font the page loads: elsewhere the page falls back to Segoe UI or the system sans and loses most of its character. The captures were taken on macOS.
Captured 300 ms after load the table still shows all seven lines (`media/desktop-full-at-load.png`); the other stills are taken after the fold.
